packet_dag.terminal_condition: The signed Rabbi provider session uses the OneTime scoped section model, shows no generic provider setup diagnostics as normal content, exposes only role-appropriate CRM/mailbox/communications/content/classroom/user/support/WhatsApp actions, and passes focused tests plus deploy/live smoke.

title: OneTime Rabbi Provider Session UI Cleanup

reasons: The operator reported that the Rabbi portal showed random configured/not-configured information instead of a clean CRM/action workspace.
The objective requires logging in as Rabbi Scheller and seeing a production-ready OneTime provider portal.
The implementation is limited to the signed provider session UI and does not perform external provider sends.
likely_external_provider_blockers: Real WAPI send remains blocked until Rabbi WAPI credentials and class-link environment are supplied.
ramble_router.next_exact_packet: After this packet deploys, run the Agent Mode Rabbi provider prompt against the live route and ingest the Operations dropoff.

operator_intent_summary: When Shloimie or Rabbi Scheller opens the actual signed Rabbi provider account, the portal should feel like a OneTimeOneTime production workspace: scoped black/yellow brand, clean CRM/mailbox/communications actions, consistent side navigation, no BNA Academy bleed, no test labels, and no generic Super Admin setup diagnostics as the normal Rabbi experience.
raw_quotes: I want to log in as Rabbi Scheller and see exactly what it looks like
there should be no like cards that have random information
there shouldn't be any overlap between The Branding of BNA and one time mishna
I wasn't able to even see the actual rabbi's CRM and where his emails are stored
just be clear buttons and actions that actually do things
out_of_scope: No payment, access grant, DNS, Zoom, Vimeo, Drive, or external provider mutation.
No broad redesign of parent/student/member/classroom routes.
affected_surfaces: Provider communications and WhatsApp setup sections

observed: Review/view-as mode already uses a Rabbi-facing OneTime section model.
The signed provider session still falls through to the generic provider section model.
Generic provider session sections include commercial, integrations, access, API usage, settings, Google Business, upgrade, and other setup-oriented surfaces that read like Super Admin diagnostics.
Review fallbacks still use TEST labels, but signed provider mode must not use TEST fallback labels.
known_blockers: Live WAPI send remains blocked by missing Rabbi WAPI credential folder/token and class-link env.

expanded_phrases.million-dollar app: For this packet: role-scoped navigation, compact action-first sections, no test labels in signed provider mode, no cross-brand bleed, and deploy/live-smoke evidence.
expanded_phrases.launch-ready: The signed provider route should be safe for Rabbi/Shloimie to open without seeing test harness language or super-admin-only setup diagnostics.
expanded_phrases.professional: Visible Rabbi sections should use concise headings and action labels: CRM, Mailbox, Messages, Content, Live Class, Library, WhatsApp, Users, Badges, Support.
expanded_phrases.CRM: The provider CRM section must show parent/student/support/message context and routes to mailbox/draft actions without exposing backend diagnostics.
expanded_phrases.configured: Configuration states must not appear as standalone Rabbi-facing cards unless the Rabbi can perform a clear role-appropriate action from that card.
expanded_phrases.working: Every visible button either navigates, opens a safe preview, saves a draft/setup record, or is explicitly blocked by missing external setup.
expanded_phrases.clean: For this packet, clean means the signed Rabbi portal shows only role-relevant OneTime sections and action cards, with no generic setup diagnostics as normal workspace content.
expanded_phrases.random information: Generic commercial/integration/access/API/debug cards are removed from the signed Rabbi section model.
expanded_phrases.BNA bleed: Signed provider mode uses OneTime branding and must not show BNA Academy language or Hebrew/English public-site toggles.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: Use the existing first-party provider portal and OneTime review/view-as section model; do not add GHL/LeadConnector or any new external CRM runtime.

requirements.statement: The signed Rabbi provider session must use the OneTime scoped section model instead of the generic provider setup model.
requirements.expected_result: The normal Rabbi session sidebar/top actions show CRM, Mailbox, Messages, Content, Live Class, Library, WhatsApp, Users, Badges, and Support; generic commercial/integration/access/API/settings cards are not normal Rabbi sections.
acceptance_criteria: Visible signed-provider body contains no TEST label.
Visible signed-provider CRM body contains no configured/not configured diagnostics.
WhatsApp setup remains action-gated and no-send.
